questions.passage: For the festival, villagers ______ every doorway with garlands of marigolds, and children hang paper lanterns from the branches of the trees along the main street.

questions.passage: The study concerned only a single species of frog. Its ______ are far wider, however: if the same chemical affects other amphibians in the same way, wetlands across the continent may be at risk.
questions.explanation: Possible wider effects of the finding are its implications.

distractors.why: Misnomers are wrong names, which does not fit.
Subterfuges are tricks, which does not fit.
Bulwarks are defenses, which does not fit.

definition: a state of confusion, disorder, or great worry

examples.text: The king's sudden death threw the court into turmoil.
Her calm face hides the turmoil she feels.
The kitchen was in turmoil an hour before the guests arrived.

confused.note: Turmoil is confusion and disorder; toil is hard work.

questions.passage: The announcement that the factory would close threw the town into ______. Shops shut early, families held hurried meetings, and a crowd gathered outside the mayor's office demanding to know what would happen next.
questions.explanation: Hurried meetings and anxious crowds show confusion and worry.

distractors.why: Foresight is planning ahead, which does not describe the scene.
Prowess is great skill, which does not fit.
Solace is comfort, the opposite of the town's distress.

definition: to get something from a source

examples.text: The drug is derived from the bark of a tropical tree.
The word "salary" derives from the Latin for salt.
I derive great satisfaction from crossing things off a list.

confused.note: To derive is to get from a source; to deprive is to take something away.

questions.passage: Many common medicines are ______ from plants. Aspirin, for instance, was first made from a compound found in willow bark, which healers had used against fever for thousands of years.
questions.explanation: Being made from a compound in willow bark is coming from a source.

distractors.why: Distorted means twisted out of shape, which does not fit.
Replenished means refilled, which does not fit.
Surpassed means exceeded, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin rivus, "stream": to draw off from a stream

definition: lasting or continuing for a long time; happening again and again

examples.text: Perennial plants return each spring without replanting.
Flooding was a perennial problem in the lower town.
Who gets the window seat is a perennial argument in our car.

confused.note: A perennial plant lives for many years; an annual lives for one.

questions.passage: The shortage of parking near the stadium is a ______ complaint. It has been raised at nearly every council meeting for thirty years, and each new mayor has promised, without success, to solve it.
questions.explanation: A complaint raised for thirty years keeps recurring.

distractors.why: Nascent means just beginning, the opposite of a decades-old complaint.
Opportune means well timed, which does not fit.
Notable means remarkable; the point is how long the complaint has lasted.

partsNote: from Latin annus, "year": through the years

definition: to be better or greater than something or someone

examples.text: The new telescope surpasses its predecessor in every measure.
The city's wealth soon surpassed that of the capital.
This year's bake sale surpassed our goal by two hundred dollars.

confused.note: To surpass is to exceed; to suppress is to hold down.

questions.passage: The apprentice did not merely equal her teacher. Within ten years she had ______ him, producing violins whose tone many players judged the finest ever made.
questions.explanation: Making finer violins than her teacher is being better than he was.

distractors.why: Reiterated means repeated, which does not fit.
Distorted means twisted, which does not fit.
Disavowed means denied connection with, which does not fit.

partsNote: from French passer, "to pass": to pass above

definition: moving, reacting, or working more slowly than normal

examples.text: Cold temperatures make reptiles sluggish and slow to react.
Trade remained sluggish for a decade after the war.
I feel sluggish all morning if I skip breakfast.

confused.note: Sluggish is the adjective meaning slow; a sluggard is a lazy person.

questions.passage: In summer the river runs fast and clear. By late autumn, when little rain has fallen for months, it becomes ______, creeping between its banks so slowly that leaves on the surface seem not to move.
questions.explanation: A river creeping so slowly that leaves seem still is moving slowly.

distractors.why: Frenetic means wildly fast, the opposite of this river.
Preposterous means absurd, which does not fit.
Genial means friendly, which does not fit.

definition: the ability to predict what will happen and to plan for it

examples.text: The queen's foresight in storing grain saved the city during the siege.
The engineers had the foresight to build the bridge wider than was then needed.
I had the foresight to bring a second charger.

confused.note: Foresight is seeing what will be needed before it happens; hindsight is understanding only afterward.

questions.passage: The town's founders showed remarkable ______. A century before anyone owned a car, they laid out streets thirty meters wide, and the city has never needed to demolish a building to ease its traffic.
questions.explanation: Planning for needs a century ahead is predicting and preparing for the future.

distractors.why: Turmoil is disorder, which does not fit.
Subterfuge is trickery, which does not fit.
Credence is belief, which does not fit.

definition: completely unreasonable or ridiculous

examples.text: The idea that the tiny duchy could invade the empire was preposterous.
The duke wears a preposterous hat shaped like a ship.
It is preposterous to charge nine dollars for a bottle of water.

confused.note: Preposterous means absurd; prosperous means wealthy and successful.

questions.passage: The claim that the pyramid was built in a single year is ______. Moving its two million blocks in that time would have required setting one in place every fifteen seconds, day and night.
questions.explanation: A claim that requires an impossible pace is ridiculous.

distractors.why: Notable means worthy of attention, which does not capture absurdity.
Pithy means brief and meaningful, which does not fit.
Opportune means well timed, which does not fit.

partsNote: with the back part in front

definition: to say something again, usually for emphasis

examples.text: The envoy reiterated his king's demand for the return of the port.
The authors reiterate that their findings apply only to adults.
Let me reiterate: do not feed the dog chocolate.

confused.note: To iterate is to repeat a process; to reiterate is to say again for emphasis.

questions.passage: The minister had already stated twice that taxes would not rise. Pressed again by reporters, she ______ the promise in the same words, adding only that she did not know how to make it any clearer.
questions.explanation: Stating the promise again in the same words is repeating it.

distractors.why: Disavowed means denied, the opposite of repeating a promise.
Distorted means twisted, which does not fit.
Derived means obtained from a source, which does not fit.

definition: not moving or not able to move; not reacting chemically

examples.text: Helium is inert and will not burn or combine with other elements.
The dog lies inert in the sun, ignoring every squirrel.
After the holiday meal, the whole family sat inert on the couch.

confused.note: Inert means motionless or unreactive; inept means unskilled.

questions.passage: Gold does not rust or tarnish because it is chemically ______. Unlike iron or copper, it does not react with air or water, which is why coins recovered after centuries on the seabed still shine.
questions.explanation: A metal that does not react with air or water is chemically inactive.

distractors.why: Frenetic means frantically active, which does not fit a metal.
Facile means too easy or shallow, which does not fit.
Perennial means long-lasting; the sentence explains that gold does not react.

partsNote: from Latin ars, "skill": without skill or activity

definition: to change the shape, sound, or meaning of something so that it is no longer true or clear

examples.text: The curved glass distorts the image at its edges.
Later chroniclers distorted the story to flatter their own kings.
The cheap speakers distort every song into a buzz.

confused.note: To distort is to twist out of shape or truth; to extort is to obtain by threats.

questions.passage: The senator complained that the newspaper had ______ her remarks. She had said that the plan "deserved study"; the headline reported that she had "thrown her support behind" it.
questions.explanation: Reporting cautious words as full support twists their meaning.

distractors.why: Reiterated means repeated accurately, but the paper changed her meaning.
Broached means raised a subject, which does not fit.
Surpassed means exceeded, which does not fit.

definition: to fill something again or bring it back to its former level

examples.text: Spring rains replenish the aquifer that the city draws on all summer.
The army paused for a week to replenish its supplies.
I replenished the snack drawer before my friends came over.

confused.note: To replenish is to refill; to relinquish is to give up.

questions.passage: The lake has shrunk by half in ten years. Scientists say that only several winters of heavy snow in the mountains could ______ it, and no such winters are forecast.
questions.explanation: Heavy snowmelt would fill the lake again.

distractors.why: Distort means to twist out of shape, which does not fit.
Derive means to obtain from a source, which does not fit "it."
Perceive means to notice, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin plenus, "full": to make full again
